title: Sickle cell variants, hemolytic and aplastic anemia, hemophilia, neutropenia
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's blood disorder (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for hemophilia A.

HPI: (Copied Forward)
The patient is a 56-year-old male with a known history of hemophilia A (hereditary factor VIII deficiency). He is currently managed on a prophylactic factor infusion regimen. He reports consistent adherence to the infusion schedule and denies any significant complications related to his condition. He is stable on his current treatment plan.

(Update)
Today the patient presents for a scheduled follow-up. He reports that he has been feeling well since the last visit. He maintains his routine of prophylactic infusions as directed. He denies any new symptoms or concerns regarding his factor VIII deficiency. He continues to engage in light physical activity without issues.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, RR 16, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F, Weight 195 lbs.

Recent Labs:
Hemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.1 x 10^9/L
Platelet Count: 210 x 10^9/L
Factor VIII Level: 15% (pre-infusion)

Medication List:
- Factor VIII concentrate (prophylactic infusions)
- Multivitamin daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for weight loss, fatigue, or chills.
Skin: Negative for rashes or bruising.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain or stiffness.
Neurological: Negative for headaches or dizziness.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath or cough.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.

Social History:
The patient is a non-smoker. He works full-time in a sedentary office environment. He lives with his spouse and two children. He reports regular exercise and a balanced diet.

Family History:
Father: History of hemophilia A.
Mother: Healthy.
Siblings: One brother with known factor VIII deficiency.

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3. In no acute distress.
Skin: No active lesions or bruising noted.
Musculoskeletal: Full range of motion in all major joints. No swelling or tenderness noted in the knees or elbows.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. S1, S2 heard. No murmurs.
Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.

Assessment:
1. Hemophilia A: Patient is stable on his current prophylactic factor infusion schedule.

Plan:
1. Continue current prophylactic factor VIII infusions as prescribed.
2. Maintain current monitoring schedule.
3. Return to clinic in 6 months for routine follow-up.

Electronically signed,
A. Rivera, MD
October 14, 2026
explanations: Hemophilia A, hereditary factor VIII deficiency: D66 (HCC 111, the 'male' hemophilia HCC).
